human_owner.summary: Approved in advance by the owner through auto mode; the Claude reviewer decides.

non_blocking_findings.finding: The quadriceps hold the knees straight in the toe-supported plank, but only vastus lateralis and rectus_femoris would appear through postural or hip demands. They are currently explicit zeros. This is minor and does not change the muscle pattern that matters for this exercise.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Optionally consider anti_extension_hip or postural_stabilization to credit lower-body isometric support in a future revision.

non_blocking_findings.finding: wrist_stability only applies once the hands are loaded at the top of the movement. This does not matter for a bodyweight press-up.

model_reviewer.summary: The frozen definition fits the source. Frame 1 shows the forearms on the floor with the torso rigid. Frame 2 shows the arms extended with the hands on the floor. Elbow extension is the only joint that moves under load, so a single primary elbow_joint/extension action is right. All three triceps heads come out as primary movers and anconeus as a synergist. The shoulder angle stays roughly constant between the two positions, so shoulder_position_hold is a better fit than a listed shoulder action. The trunk stays rigid, so anti_extension_spine and pelvic_alignment are the correct way to credit the core. The hips and hamstrings also appear as stabilizers. Bilateral laterality, closed_chain and the movement-family labels are all appropriate.
